title: Budgeting when income changes
description: Freelance, part-time, and seasonal work rarely pay the same each month — here is how to budget anyway.

body.heading: Budget from your low month
paragraphs: If your income varies, base your essential budget on a low month, not your best month. List the must-pay costs that fit inside that low figure. That way, even a quiet month is covered.
In better months, the extra is not a surprise party — it is your chance to build a buffer, save, or pay for irregular costs like annual fees or repairs.

body.heading: Build a buffer first
paragraphs: A buffer is a small cushion of money kept for lean weeks. Start with a modest goal, like covering one week of essentials, and grow it slowly. A buffer turns an irregular income from stressful into manageable.
Keep the buffer separate from everyday spending money if you can, so it is still there when you need it.

body.heading: Review monthly
paragraphs: Variable income means a monthly five-minute review matters more, not less. Look at what came in, what is due soon, and move money to the buffer or bills before spending the rest.

takeaway: When income varies, budget from your low month and let good months build your buffer.
